# 16-Mask CMOS Process

Step-by-step fabrication of a CMOS pair (PMOS in N-well, NMOS in P-well) on a P-substrate. Each patterning step uses photoresist and a mask. Images are in the `images/` folder and follow the order of the process.

---

## 1. Active region definition (Mask 1)

The wafer gets a stack of ~40 nm SiO2, ~80 nm Si3N4 and ~1 µm photoresist. UV light is shone through **Mask 1**, so the resist is exposed only in selected areas. After developing, the resist protects the areas where transistors will be (active regions).

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

---

## 2. Field oxide (LOCOS)

Nitride that is not protected by resist is etched away. The wafer is then oxidised, and thick **field oxide** grows only where there is no nitride. This isolates the transistors from each other. The process is called **LOCOS** (Local Oxidation of Silicon). The oxide grows slightly under the nitride edges, which is called the **bird's beak**.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

---

## 3. N-well and P-well formation (Mask 3)

Wells are made so that both types of transistor can sit on one wafer: PMOS needs an n-type body (N-well) and NMOS needs a p-type body (P-well). Photoresist (patterned with **Mask 3**) blocks the dopants from regions where the well is not wanted, and the implant forms the wells in the substrate.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

---

## Threshold voltage reference

`Vt = Vto + γ ( √|−2Φf + Vsb| − √|−2Φf| )`

- **Vto**: threshold voltage at Vsb = 0 (depends on the manufacturing process)
- **γ**: body effect coefficient
- **Φf**: Fermi potential
- **Vsb**: source-to-body voltage; increasing it increases Vt (body effect)

When Vgs reaches Vt, the surface under the gate inverts to n-type and a channel forms between source and drain.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

---

## 4. Gate formation

**Gate oxide:** the original oxide is stripped with dilute **HF**, then a fresh, high quality oxide (~10 nm) is grown. A thin layer in the channel region is doped (N / P marked in the figure) to set the threshold voltage.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

**Gate patterning (Mask 6):** polysilicon is deposited over the oxide, resist is applied and **Mask 6** defines the gate. The poly is etched so only the gates remain.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

---

## 5. Lightly doped drain (LDD) formation

A light implant is done on both sides of each gate. **P-** implant goes into the N-well (PMOS) and **N-** implant goes into the P-well (NMOS), with resist covering the other device each time. The gate itself blocks the implant, so the regions align with the gate edge (self-aligned). LDD reduces the electric field at the drain edge.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

---

## 6. Source and drain formation

Spacers (green) are formed on the sidewalls of the gate. A heavy implant then creates **P+** source/drain in the N-well and **N+** source/drain in the P-well. The spacer keeps the LDD region next to the channel lightly doped.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

---

## 7. Contacts and local interconnects

A titanium based layer is formed on the source, drain and gate top (dark blue) to give low resistance contacts. The unwanted **TiN** is etched away using **RCA cleaning**, so the contact layer stays only where needed.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

---

## 8. Higher level metal formation

### 8.1 Insulating layer

~1 µm of SiO2 doped with phosphorus or boron (phosphosilicate glass / borophosphosilicate glass) is deposited over the whole wafer. This insulates the transistors from the metal above.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

### 8.2 Planarization

**CMP** (Chemical Mechanical Polishing) flattens the wafer surface so the next layers can be patterned properly.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

### 8.3 Contact plugs

Contact holes are opened down to the source, drain and gate, lined with a thin layer (pink) and filled with metal plugs (blue). **CMP** is done again to remove the extra metal and flatten the surface.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

### 8.4 Metal 1 deposition

An **aluminum (Al)** layer is deposited on top of the flat surface.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

### 8.5 Metal 1 patterning

The Al is **plasma etched** using a patterned resist, leaving metal lines that connect to the plugs below.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

### 8.6 Inter-metal oxide

**SiO2** is deposited over the metal lines and polished flat with **CMP**.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

### 8.7 Vias

Holes (vias) are etched down to Metal 1 and **TiN** is deposited as the liner inside them.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

### 8.8 Metal 2 (Mask 15)

The vias are filled with metal plugs, and another Al layer is deposited. **Mask 15** is used to define the Metal 2 pattern.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

### 8.9 Top protection layer

A top dielectric layer of **Si3N4** is deposited to protect the chip.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

---

## 9. Final device

The metal layers bring out the **Source (S), Gate (G) and Drain (D)** terminals of both transistors. This completes the fabrication of the CMOS pair.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="700">

---

## Keywords

LOCOS, bird's beak, N-well, P-well, gate oxide, polysilicon, LDD, spacer, source/drain implant, CMP, plug, via, passivation
